title: Secrets lifecycle and audit orchestration notes
content:
Purpose:
This document captures an engineering-first approach to orchestrating secrets lifecycle, KMS/HSM bindings, and immutable audit forwarding for private (VPC / on-prem) Redwood deployments. It is intentionally a working draft for discussion with infra, security, and release engineering ahead of a phased Terraform refactor + upgrade rollout.

Scope:
- Customer-managed KMS integrations (cloud KMS + external HSMs via KMIP/PKCS11)
- Local secrets storage patterns for control plane and worker nodes
- Terraform module changes for secret provisioning, rotation, and audit-config
- Audit log capture, signing, and secure forwarding to customer SIEMs or Redwood-managed retention
- Backwards-compatible upgrade paths for existing on-prem stacks

Goals:
- Ensure key material never leaves customer boundary unless explicitly allowed; prefer enveloping with customer KMS/HSM
- Enable automated credential rotation with zero-downtime rollouts for inference services
- Provide verifiable, tamper-evident audit records for all secret operations (create/read/rotate/revoke)
- Make Terraform modules idempotent and easy to reason about during upgrades

Assumptions / Constraints:
- Target environments: air-gapped on-prem, customer VPCs with restricted egress, and hybrid datacenters
- Some customers will only allow HSM-backed keys (FIPS/HSM requirement)
- Ops teams may have limited ability to run additional agents; prefer minimal new daemons

High-level architecture (textual):
1) Customer KMS/HSM (primary key source) -> encryption keys used to envelop Redwood service keys.
2) Ondeploy: Terraform provisions a "secrets-controller" service (small k8s deployment or systemd unit) that holds ephemeral service identities and communicates with KMS via customer-provided connector.
3) Secrets controller creates per-service data keys (DEKs) encrypted with customer KEK (KMS/HSM) and stores ciphertext in local secure storage (e.g., Vault, sealed secrets store, or an encrypted blob in S3-like object store).
4) Audit pipeline: every KMS/HSM request plus local secret operations are logged locally, signed by an audit signing key kept in HSM or a dedicated audit-signing KMS key, and forwarded to customer SIEM or retained in immutable object storage with append-only ACLs.

Terraform module notes (intent + variables to add):
- Module: redwood_private_secret_controller
  - intent: create secret-controller namespace, service account, IAM bindings, and secret envelope placeholders
  - new variables: customer_kms_backend (enum: gcp_kms|aws_kms|hsm_kmip|hsm_pkcs11|azure_keyvault), kms_endpoint, kms_auth_method, audit_forward_endpoint, allow_remote_key_export (bool default false)
  - outputs: secret_controller_id, encrypted_dek_reference
- Module: redwood_hsm_connector
  - intent: deploy light-weight connector process that translates KMIP/PKCS11 into internal RPC used by controller
  - variables: hsm_vendor, hsm_endpoint, hsm_trust_bundle_id, hsm_admin_user (sensitive), connector_mode (agent|sidecar|proxy)
- Module: redwood_audit_pipeline
  - intent: create delivery configuration for audit logs (forwarders, retention buckets, signing-key bindings)
  - variables: audit_bucket_path, signing_key_ref, forward_to_siem (bool), forward_url, retention_days

Migration / upgrade plan (high level steps):
Phase 0: discovery and gating
- Inventory: run terraform state inspection and small agent to enumerate existing secrets and their storage locations (Vault, Kubernetes secrets, plaintext in config maps) (JIRA-PI-3421).
- Stakeholder signoff: compliance, customer security, SRE.

Phase 1: deploy secrets-controller in listen-only mode
- Deploy controller that can read but not rotate existing secrets. Controller writes audit events to local append-only store but does not modify DEKs. This ensures visibility without risk.

Phase 2: envelope migration
- For each service, create new DEK, encrypt with customer KEK, and write DEK ciphertext to storage alongside an audit record. Rotate service to read new DEK. Provide fallback to old key for 7 days.
- Terraform change: add lifecycle ignore_changes on legacy secret resources until fully decommissioned.

Phase 3: HSM binding and audit signing
- If customer requests HSM-backed signing, deploy hsm_connector (agent/sidecar) and bind audit-signing key to HSM. All audit entries must be signed by HSM key.

Phase 4: validation and cutover
- Run smoke and traffic tests. Execute chaos scenarios (simulate KMS latency, drop connector) and verify fallback policies.
- Decommission legacy secrets and remove ignore_changes.

Key rotation patterns and operational details:
- Rotation cadence: default weekly for short-lived service DEKs, monthly for KEK metadata, annual for master root keys (customer policy dependent).
- Plan for automated rotation orchestrator (stateless cron job managed by Terraform) that: 1) creates new DEK, 2) re-encrypts service metadata, 3) signals services via rollout webhook to re-init.
- Rollback: maintain previous DEK ciphertext for N days (configurable per customer) and provide immediate secret rebind if new key fails validation.

HSM integration specifics (notes to engineering):
- Preferred transports: KMIP over TLS for vendor-agnostic; PKCS#11 only if customer provides local socket/device access.
- Connector modes: sidecar (lowest latency, per-node), agent (single host-local), or proxy (centralized within customer network). Tradeoffs: sidecar scales with pods but increases surface area; proxy centralizes auditing but is a single point to harden.
- Authentication: use mutual TLS with mTLS certs provisioned via Terraform from customer CAs, or use short-lived tokens provisioned from on-prem identity provider.

Audit log design:
- Event model: {timestamp, actor, action, target, request_id, keystore_ref, result_code, signature}
- Signing: prefer HSM-signed hashes of batched events to reduce HSM ops. Keep per-batch Merkle root recorded in append-only store.
- Forwarding model: push to customer SIEM over TLS with mTLS or to an object store with signed manifests. Include guaranteed delivery retries and a poison-queue for failed events.
- Retention & immutability: recommend write-once buckets with versioning and retention policies; optionally ship digest to external notarization service (customer choice).

Testing plan (minimum):
- Unit tests for terraform modules (terraform validate + terratest stubs)
- Integration: spin up a small onprem replica in CI that exercises KMIP connector using soft-HSM (SoftHSM v2)
- Chaos tests: simulate HSM unavailable, slow KMS, corrupted audit batch
- Compliance tests: replay-signed-audit verification tool to validate signature chain

Operational runbooks (short-form):
- Emergency key compromise: immediate revoke on KEK, create new DEKs with new KEK, trigger rolling rebind via orchestrator; notify security and affected customers with timeline template in Confluence.
- Audit discrepancy: quarantine events, snapshot object store, run signature verification, if mismatch escalate to oncall and compliance.

Open questions / decision items (to resolve in sync):
- Do we require all customers to provide a dedicated audit endpoint, or do we allow Redwood-managed retention for customers who opt in?
- Connector deployment model: should sidecar be default for k8s customers? (tradeoffs: bootstrap complexity vs latency)
- Default rotation cadence and backward-compatible retention window (7 vs 14 days)

Action items (owners):
- Priya: draft terraform variable schema and publish RFC to infra-terraform channel (due 2025-02-20)
- Ethan: prototype KMIP connector in Go using gokmip library and run against SoftHSM (POC by 2025-02-28)
- Luis: design audit forwarding module and S3 retention layout; include immutability options (due 2025-03-05)
- Maya: coordinate compliance review and prepare checklist for customer-facing guide (due 2025-03-10)

References and helpful links:
- Internal: CONFLUENCE-1234 (private-deploy-security-brief)
- Upstream libs: https://github.com/OpenKMIP/gokmip, https://github.com/opendnssec/softHSMv2
- Related Terraform modules: github.com/redwood-inference/terraform-modules/secret-lifecycle

Notes to self / rough todos:

- Add example terraform usage snippet showing how to set customer_kms_backend=hsm_kmip
- Verify legal wording for audit forwarding across regions

Status: WIP — looking for feedback on the migration phases and Terraform variable choices.
